# Workforce Security Training Standard

**Organization:** Example Org
**Owning Team:** Security Awareness
**Classification:** Internal — Mandatory Compliance

## 1. Purpose

This Standard establishes the requirements for Example Org's workforce security and privacy awareness and training program. It defines the policy, procedures, training content, delivery cadence, and documentation obligations that security and IT staff must implement and against which compliance will be audited. The Security Awareness team is accountable for this process end to end, including all handoffs to participating teams.

## 2. Scope

This Standard applies to all members of the Example Org workforce, including management, senior executives, employees, and contractors, and to all individuals working on behalf of the organization who access, use, manage, or develop organizational systems.

## 3. Awareness and Training Policy and Procedures

### 3.1 Policy Development and Dissemination

Security Awareness shall develop, document, and disseminate to organization-defined personnel or roles an awareness and training policy that addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance, and that is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines. While NIST permits the policy to be organization-level, mission/business process-level, or system-level, this Standard adopts an organization-level policy. [NIST AT-1 | ARC-AMPE AT-1]

### 3.2 Procedures

Security Awareness shall develop, document, and disseminate procedures to facilitate implementation of the awareness and training policy and the associated awareness and training controls. [NIST AT-1 | ARC-AMPE AT-1]

### 3.3 Designated Official

The lead of the Security Awareness team is the designated official responsible for managing the development, documentation, and dissemination of the awareness and training policy and procedures. [NIST AT-1 | ARC-AMPE AT-1]

### 3.4 Policy and Procedure Review

Security Awareness shall review and update the awareness and training policy at least annually and following organization-defined events. [NIST AT-1 | ARC-AMPE AT-1]

Security Awareness shall review and update the awareness and training procedures at least annually and following organization-defined events. [NIST AT-1 | ARC-AMPE AT-1]

### 3.5 Monitoring of Applicable Changes

Security Awareness shall actively monitor for changes to applicable privacy laws, regulations, and overarching policy that affect awareness and training policies. [ARC-AMPE AT-1]

### 3.6 Life Cycle Coverage

Security Awareness shall ensure awareness and training policies and procedures support cybersecurity and privacy safeguards to the greatest extent feasible throughout the system's life cycle and the life cycle of the information on that system. [ARC-AMPE AT-1]

## 4. Documentation and Records Management

### 4.1 Written Maintenance

Security Awareness shall maintain the policies and procedures implemented under this Standard in written form (which may be electronic), and shall maintain a written (electronic permitted) record of any action, activity, or assessment required to be documented. [HIPAA 164.316(b)(1)]

### 4.2 Retention

Security Awareness shall retain required documentation for 6 years from the date of its creation or the date it was last in effect, whichever is later. [HIPAA 164.316(b)(2)(i)]

### 4.3 Availability

Security Awareness shall make documentation available to those persons responsible for implementing the procedures to which the documentation pertains. [HIPAA 164.316(b)(2)(ii)]

### 4.4 Periodic Review and Update

Security Awareness shall review documentation periodically and update it as needed in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of electronic protected health information. [HIPAA 164.316(b)(2)(iii)]

## 5. Security Awareness and Literacy Training

### 5.1 Program Implementation

Example Org shall implement a security awareness and training program for all members of the workforce, including management. The Security Awareness team owns and operates this program. [HIPAA 164.308(a)(5)(i)]

### 5.2 Initial and Refresher Literacy Training

Security Awareness shall provide security and privacy literacy training to system users (including managers, senior executives, and contractors) as part of initial training for new users and thereafter at least annually. [NIST AT-2 | ARC-AMPE AT-2]

### 5.3 Event-Driven Literacy Training

Security Awareness shall provide additional literacy training when required by system changes or following organization-defined events (e.g., assessment or audit findings; security or privacy incidents; changes to applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines). [NIST AT-2 | ARC-AMPE AT-2]

### 5.4 Awareness Techniques

Security Awareness shall employ techniques to increase the security and privacy awareness of system users, per organization-defined awareness techniques; these techniques shall include phishing email tests and other organization-defined techniques. Phishing exercises shall be conducted through the [Phishing Simulation Platform], and their outcomes recorded as Phishing simulation results. [NIST AT-2 | ARC-AMPE AT-2]

### 5.5 Content Updates

Security Awareness shall update literacy training and awareness content at least annually and following organization-defined events. [NIST AT-2 | ARC-AMPE AT-2]

### 5.6 Lessons Learned

Security Awareness shall incorporate lessons learned from internal or external security incidents or breaches into literacy training and awareness techniques. [NIST AT-2 | ARC-AMPE AT-2]

### 5.7 Education and Awareness Training Program Coverage

Security Awareness shall develop and implement an information security and privacy education and awareness training program for all employees and individuals working on behalf of the organization who access, use, manage, or develop systems; this program may be integrated with general cybersecurity training. [ARC-AMPE AT-2]

### 5.8 Sensitive Information in Email

Security Awareness shall include, within the information security and privacy education and awareness training, an individual's responsibilities associated with sending sensitive information in email. [ARC-AMPE AT-2]

### 5.9 Privacy Training Prior to Access

Security Awareness shall provide privacy training before granting access to organizational systems and networks, for all employees and contractors, for all systems that collect, maintain, store, use, or disclose Personally Identifiable Information (PII). [ARC-AMPE AT-2]

## 6. Specialized Literacy Training Topics

### 6.1 Practical Exercises

Security Awareness shall provide practical exercises in literacy training that simulate events and incidents. [NIST AT-2(1)]

### 6.2 Insider Threat

Security Awareness shall provide literacy training on recognizing and reporting potential indicators of insider threat. This training should include how to communicate employee and management concerns regarding potential insider threat indicators through appropriate organizational channels in accordance with established organizational policies and procedures. [NIST AT-2(2) | ARC-AMPE AT-2(2)]

### 6.3 Social Engineering and Social Mining

Security Awareness shall provide literacy training on recognizing and reporting potential and actual instances of social engineering and social mining. This training should include how to recognize and report, through appropriate organizational and defined channels (e.g., applicable security and privacy plans), potential attempts to trick an individual into revealing information or taking an action that can be used to breach, compromise, or otherwise adversely impact a system. [NIST AT-2(3) | ARC-AMPE AT-2(3)]

### 6.4 Suspicious Communications and Anomalous Behavior

Security Awareness shall provide literacy training on recognizing suspicious communications and anomalous behavior in organizational systems using organization-defined indicators of malicious code. This training should include how to recognize and report, through appropriate organizational and defined channels (e.g., applicable security and privacy plans): potentially suspicious email or web communications (e.g., receiving an unexpected email, receiving an email containing strange or poor grammar, or receiving an email from an unfamiliar sender who appears to be from a known sponsor or contractor), and anomalous behaviors in systems. [NIST AT-2(4) | ARC-AMPE AT-2(4)]

### 6.5 Advanced Persistent Threat

Security Awareness shall provide literacy training on the advanced persistent threat (APT). This training should include techniques for recognizing suspicious emails, use of removable systems in non-secure settings, the potential targeting of individuals at home, and the various ways APTs can infiltrate the organization (e.g., through websites, emails, advertisement pop-ups, articles, and social engineering). [NIST AT-2(5) | ARC-AMPE AT-2(5)]

### 6.6 Cyber Threat Environment

Security Awareness shall provide literacy training on the cyber threat environment and reflect current cyber threat information in system operations. [NIST AT-2(6)]

## 7. Ongoing Security Practices

### 7.1 Security Updates and Reminders

Security Awareness shall implement periodic security updates (security reminders). [HIPAA 164.308(a)(5)(ii)(A)]

### 7.2 Malicious Software

Security Awareness shall implement procedures for guarding against, detecting, and reporting malicious software. [HIPAA 164.308(a)(5)(ii)(B)]

### 7.3 Log-In Monitoring

Security Awareness shall implement procedures for monitoring log-in attempts and reporting discrepancies. [HIPAA 164.308(a)(5)(ii)(C)]

### 7.4 Password Practices

Security Awareness shall implement procedures for creating, changing, and safeguarding passwords. [HIPAA 164.308(a)(5)(ii)(D)]

## 8. Role-Based Security and Privacy Training

### 8.1 Initial and Refresher Role-Based Training

Security Awareness shall provide role-based security and privacy training to personnel with organization-defined roles and responsibilities before authorizing access to the system or information or performing assigned duties, and thereafter at least annually. This requirement applies to significant information security and privacy roles. [NIST AT-3 | ARC-AMPE AT-3]

### 8.2 Event-Driven Role-Based Training

Security Awareness shall provide role-based security and privacy training when required by system changes; when an employee enters a new position that requires additional role-specific training; and when significant information system or system environment changes occur. [NIST AT-3 | ARC-AMPE AT-3]

### 8.3 Content Updates

Security Awareness shall update role-based training content at least annually and following significant changes to the system or the system environment. [NIST AT-3 | ARC-AMPE AT-3]

### 8.4 Lessons Learned

Security Awareness shall incorporate lessons learned from internal or external security incidents or breaches into role-based training. [NIST AT-3 | ARC-AMPE AT-3]

### 8.5 Access Enforcement for Training Compliance

Security Awareness shall disable the user accounts of employees and contractors with significant information security and privacy roles and responsibilities who have not completed the required role-based training within the mandated timeframes, until they have met the role-based training requirement. Account disablement shall be coordinated with the [Identity Provider] administrators. [ARC-AMPE AT-3]

### 8.6 Environmental Controls Training

Security Awareness shall provide organization-defined personnel or roles with initial and annual training in the employment and operation of environmental controls. [NIST AT-3(1)]

### 8.7 Physical Security Controls Training

Security Awareness shall provide organization-defined personnel or roles with initial and annual training in the employment and operation of physical security controls. [NIST AT-3(2)]

### 8.8 Practical Exercises

Security Awareness shall provide practical exercises in security and privacy training that reinforce training objectives. [NIST AT-3(3)]

## 9. Privacy Training for PII Processing

### 9.1 PII Processing and Transparency Controls Training

Security Awareness shall provide organizational personnel (including vendors, contractors, and employees) with initial training — and thereafter at least annually — in the employment and operation of personally identifiable information processing and transparency controls. [NIST AT-3(5) | ARC-AMPE AT-3(5)]

### 9.2 Privacy Education and Awareness Program

Security Awareness shall develop and implement a privacy education and awareness training program for all employees and individuals working on behalf of the organization involved in managing, using, and/or processing PII. [ARC-AMPE AT-3(5)]

### 9.3 PII in Email

Security Awareness shall include responsibilities associated with sending PII in email within the privacy education and awareness training. [ARC-AMPE AT-3(5)]

### 9.4 Job-Specific Content

Security Awareness shall ensure privacy communications and training are job-specific and commensurate with the employee's responsibilities. [ARC-AMPE AT-3(5)]

### 9.5 Privacy Training Before Access and Annual Refresher

Security Awareness shall ensure initial training of employees (including managers) on their privacy responsibilities is completed before permitting access to organizational information and systems, with refresher training completed every one (1) year thereafter. [ARC-AMPE AT-3(5)]

### 9.6 Advanced Training

Security Awareness shall ensure any additional or advanced training provided is commensurate with the employee's responsibilities. [ARC-AMPE AT-3(5)]

## 10. Evidence, Reporting, and Accountability

### 10.1 Required Evidence

The Security Awareness team shall produce and retain the following artifacts as evidence of program operation:

| Artifact                    | Description                                                                                                                   |
| --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Training completion report  | Record of workforce completion of initial, refresher, and role-based training, maintained in the [Learning Management System] |
| Phishing simulation results | Outcomes of phishing email tests conducted under Section 5.4                                                                  |

These artifacts are subject to the retention requirement in Section 4.2.

### 10.2 Accountability

The Security Awareness team is accountable for this process end to end, including the development, delivery, tracking, review, and updating of all training and awareness activities defined in this Standard, and for the production and retention of the evidence artifacts listed in Section 10.1. Other teams participate in individual steps (e.g., [Identity Provider] administrators for account disablement under Section 8.5), but ownership of the process and its handoffs rests with Security Awareness.
